report.brief:
ARCHITECTURAL DEVELOPMENT PASS: Fundamentally redesign the original retained $25m Calypsonian House contemporary tropical waterfront mansion. The main residence is architecturally inadequate. Use your architectural knowledge to rethink overall composition, scale, primary and secondary volumes, arrival and entrance hierarchy, roof relationships, spatial organization, suite privacy, and facade depth, opening rhythm and material quality. Substantial replacement and removal of existing architecture and dependents are explicitly authorized; accessories alone do not satisfy this brief. Preserve unrelated pool/site geometry and terrain. Do not follow a supplied design template. Existing raw scene has east-terrace-rail and west-terrace-rail centres at Y=3.8 while their decks require Y=4.2; address these in your coordinated operations if retained. Original upper retreat overlaps owner/guest floors; resolve spatial allocation rather than relabeling it. Construct real hollow enclosures and connected entrances with the existing direct-scene primitives. Use only supported geometry and disclose stairs, circulation, interior, structure or other unresolved capabilities. Do not silently substitute unsupported shapes. Supply an updated architectural plan and cite actual constructed IDs for retrieved knowledge; distinguish realized work from intent. Preserve stable IDs for retained identity. No market value or construction-cost claims.
REDESIGN: Substantial changes to existing floors, walls, roofs, entrances, facades and architectural volumes are authorized. Replace or reorganize inadequate composition and spatial hierarchy, coordinating all supports and dependents in one atomic transaction. Preserve IDs for retained elements and unrelated site geometry and terrain. Explain the architectural changes and unresolved capabilities. Retrieve relevant architectural knowledge. Do not add repetitive decoration. Disclose unresolved circulation/enclosure.

explicitIntent.scaleRationale: The redesigned Calypsonian House is conceived as a substantial but disciplined waterfront residence: a tall, climate-shaded central salon is the primary social volume, with lower guest, dining, service and ocean-loggia structures forming a protected ground-level ensemble. The upper level is reduced to two separated private-suite enclosures rather than the former overlapping owner, guest and retreat floors. The ambition comes from spatial hierarchy, deep roof shelter, stone-and-timber tectonics and a deliberate arrival sequence rather than unsupported claims about cost, value or certification.
explicitIntent.arrivalAndCirculation: Arrival is organized from the north through a shallow limestone gallery and a recessed bronze entrance, then through a second bronze threshold into the double-height salon. Ground-level doors link the salon to the west guest lounge and east dining room. The ocean loggia is a sheltered outdoor room directly beyond the south salon glazing. The upper owner and guest suite slabs are structurally supported by ground-to-floor cores and are separated in plan; stairs and a fully navigable internal circulation system are not represented.
explicitIntent.volumeHierarchy: A 18m-wide, double-height limestone salon is the dominant volume and visual anchor. A lower arrival gallery gives the entrance a clear civic threshold. The west guest lounge, east dining room and northeast kitchen are deliberately lower, subordinate pavilions. Above the salon, compact owner and guest suite enclosures occupy distinct zones and are held below a single high primary roof. The ocean loggia is an outdoor extension rather than another enclosed wing.
explicitIntent.relationshipsAndViews: The principal south elevation is a broad shaded glazed opening toward the retained pool and waterfront. Smaller, more controlled glazed openings articulate the north, west and east elevations. The guest lounge and dining room each connect directly to the central salon through actual door openings, while the kitchen remains adjacent to dining. The upper suites are separated by a circulation gap and internal enclosure walls to avoid the former overlapping retreat arrangement.
explicitIntent.roofFacadeAndMaterials: A high timber flat roof expresses the primary salon and covers both upper private enclosures. Lower timber roofs shelter the gallery, guest lounge, dining/kitchen and ocean loggia. Limestone is used for substantial wall planes, ivory for private-suite partitions, bronze for doors and glazing frames, and timber for soffits, screens and outdoor shading. Deep roof edges, recessed openings and a slatted ocean screen establish tropical shade without representing unverified ventilation, drainage or weather-performance analysis.
intendedSpaces: North arrival gallery with recessed main entrance
Retained pool precinct, not redesigned in this pass

report.summary: The inadequate fragmented house is replaced by a coherent limestone-and-timber waterfront composition: a high central salon, north arrival gallery, lower guest/dining/service pavilions, sheltered ocean loggia, and two non-overlapping upper private-suite enclosures. The pool/site elements are preserved. Former elevated terrace decks and their incorrectly positioned rails are removed rather than retained, eliminating the Y=3.8 versus Y=4.2 coordination issue.
unsupported: The new-generation scene remains on the existing flat Y=0 ground plane; no terrain modification is made.
Stairs, lift, fully navigable upper-level circulation, bathrooms, closets, kitchen equipment, HVAC, drainage and structural engineering are not represented.
The upper suite floors have modeled ground-to-floor support cores, but no engineering certification is implied.

The retained pool geometry is preserved as unrelated site work; it is not re-described as a complete pool system or as a hydraulic infinity edge. Its missing north coping/basin treatment is outside this redesign scope.
Interior furniture, room fit-out, code compliance, fire egress and weather-performance simulation are unresolved.
